examples.name: Default
examples.summary: A framed widget, the workloads list, filling a panel the host sizes.

examples.name: Variants
examples.summary: A workload screen plated as a console window and bare, and a fragment framed in a console window titled with its module beside the same fragment bare on the host surface.

examples.name: Still fragment
examples.summary: The same fragment with its collaborator cursor, as a feature grid shows it, and with `:cursor="false"`, as a product band that reads like a screenshot wants it. Each fragment keeps its own plating unless `variant` asks for the other one; `width` and `fade` re-plate only the workload screens, and setting them on a fragment warns in development.

examples.name: Library
examples.summary: Every registered widget in the cell that hosts it on the site: full screens in wide panels, fragments in grid cells that play their beat on hover, framed in a console window or bare as each one is plated by default. These are the only values `name` accepts.

examples.name: Markdown
examples.summary: The same content written in a docs page: `DocMarkdown` turns a `<ConsoleMockup>` tag into a real `ConsoleMockup`. Braced attribute values are JSON, so a docs author copies them from the props or a page entry and never imports the component. `DocMarkdown` sets it in a framed 16:9 box, so the mockup has a size to fill.
